traceability.evidence:
Story file: - docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md exists and defines requirements REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE, REQ-IMPLEMENTS-VALIDATE, REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION.
Core @implements format support (REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT): - src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts: - Declares MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS = 2 documenting that a valid @implements must contain a story path and at least one requirement ID. - reportMissingImplementsValue(), reportMissingImplementsReqIds(), reportInvalidImplementsStoryPath(), reportInvalidImplementsReqId() emit detailed ESLint diagnostics for missing value, missing req IDs, invalid story path, and invalid req IDs, using messageIds "invalidImplementsFormat" and "invalidReqFormat" as described in the story. - parseImplementsTokens(...) and validateImplementsTokens(...) implement the parsing algorithm from the story: trim, split on whitespace, first token is storyPath, remaining are reqIds; they enforce MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS and validate storyPath via options.storyPattern and each reqId via options.reqPattern. - validateImplementsAnnotationHelper(...) wires parsing and validation together. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - validateImplementsAnnotation(...) constructs deps { MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS, reportMissingImplementsReqIds, reportMissingImplementsValue, reportInvalidImplementsReqId, reportInvalidImplementsStoryPath } and calls validateImplementsAnnotationHelper(...), integrating the new format into the rule. - processCommentLine(...) detects /@implements\b/ and immediately validates the value while still supporting @story and @req, which enables mixed usage of all three annotation types in a single comment. - finalizePendingAnnotation(...) still only dispatches @story and @req, preserving legacy behavior. - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts: - Header explicitly references docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md and @req REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT. - Valid tests: - "[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid single @implements with one story and one requirement (default patterns)" with code: /**\n * @implements docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE\n */ - "[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid multiple @implements lines with different stories and requirements" demonstrating multiple lines with different story paths. - "[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@implements usage in same block comment" showing all three annotations in one JSDoc. - Invalid tests around @implements: - Missing value, missing req IDs, invalid story path, invalid requirement ID, and multiple IDs where one is invalid; expectations match the detailed error messages described in the story.
Deep validation of @implements requirements (REQ-IMPLEMENTS-VALIDATE, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT): - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts: - parseImplementsLine(line: string): { storyPath: string; reqIds: string[] } | null splits the line, uses IMPLMENTS_TOKENS indices to extract storyPath and reqIds, and returns null if either is missing. The JSDoc documents REQ-IMPLEMENTS-VALIDATE, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT, REQ-SCOPED-IDS. - validateImplementsLine(opts) calls parseImplementsLine, then resolveStoryAndRequirements({ storyPath, ... }) to load a Set of requirements for that story; it then iterates reqIds and calls checkRequirementExists({ reqId, storyPath, reqSet, ... }) for each, implementing per-story requirement existence validation. - handleAnnotationLine(...) dispatches @implements lines via validateImplementsLine(...) while leaving the current storyPath unchanged, consistent with the spec that @implements is self-contained. - meta.messages includes: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" — includes the story path in the message (REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT). - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'". - docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md: - States that the rule enforces that `@req` and `@implements` reference existing requirements, that each @implements is self-contained (specifies its own story path), and that requirement IDs only need to be unique within a single story file; duplicates across files are allowed. - Provides correct and incorrect @implements examples, including missing requirement and invalid path cases. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts: - Valid tests: - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] single implements line with multiple requirements in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" with `// @implements tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-SHARED-ID REQ-ONLY-A`. - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] multi-story implements with shared requirement IDs (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" where story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md both use REQ-SHARED-ID. Both pass, confirming per-story requirement scoping. - Invalid tests: - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] missing implements requirement in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" expects an error { messageId: 'reqMissing', data: { reqId: 'REQ-NOT-IN-A', storyPath: 'tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md' } }, demonstrating deep validation and error context. - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] disallow path traversal in implements story path" expects messageId 'invalidPath' with the bad storyPath.
Update of require-* rules to accept @implements (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts (used by require-story-annotation): - commentContainsStory(comment) returns true if comment.value includes "@story" or "@implements" and is documented with REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - scanLinesForMarker(...), linesBeforeHasStory(...), parentChainHasStory(...), and fallbackTextBeforeHasStory(...) all treat lines/text containing "@story" or "@implements" as markers that the function is annotated. - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts: - Rule logic is unchanged for @story, but because it uses the helpers above, any @implements adjacent to a function satisfies the annotation presence check. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - Header includes docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - Valid case: "[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation" with code `/**\n * @implements docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED\n */\nfunction implOnly() {}` — proves @implements is sufficient for this rule. - Invalid case: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED][BACKCOMPAT] missing @story annotation on function with no @implements" shows that unannotated functions are still errors, confirming backward compatibility. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts (used by require-req-annotation via checkReqAnnotation): - commentContainsReq, linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq, and hasReqAnnotation all treat both "@req" and "@implements" as evidence of requirement annotations. JSDoc tags reference Story 010.2 and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts: - Delegates to checkReqAnnotation, which uses hasReqAnnotation; therefore, any nearby @implements satisfies the requirement annotation check. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Header includes Story 010.2 and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - Valid case: "[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation" with code `/**\n * @implements docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED\n */\nfunction implOnly() {}` — confirms @implements alone satisfies this rule. - Numerous invalid cases confirm that functions lacking both @req and @implements remain errors, preserving backward compatibility.
Requirement scoping (REQ-SCOPED-IDS): - Implementation: valid-req-reference.ts uses a per-story Set of requirement IDs (reqSet) returned by resolveStoryAndRequirements(storyPath, ...); validateImplementsLine checks each reqId only against that set, not against a global registry, so IDs can be reused across files. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md states, "Requirement IDs only need to be unique within a single story file; duplicates across different story files are allowed." This matches the story's REQ-SCOPED-IDS. - Tests: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts has a valid test where REQ-SHARED-ID appears in two different story fixtures; both @implements lines pass validation.
Error message context (REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, Acceptance Criterion: Error Messages): - valid-req-reference.ts meta.messages.reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" outputs both the missing requirement ID and the story path that was checked. - Tests for invalid @implements references (e.g., missing requirement, invalid path) assert the storyPath value in the error data, confirming behavior.
Documentation and migration guidance (Acceptance Criterion: Documentation): - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md: - Describes `@implements` alongside `@story` and `@req` and gives a concrete example using docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md. - Explains that the story path in @implements is validated with the same pattern as @story and that each requirement ID afterward is validated with the same pattern as @req. - Contains a dedicated "Migration to `@implements`" section explaining when to keep @story+@req, when to adopt @implements, and how to migrate multi-story integration functions step by step with before/after code samples. - docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md: - Documents how @implements participates in deep requirement checking and multi-story usage, and references Story 010.2 explicitly.
Testing and quality: - The relevant behavior is covered by focused ESLint RuleTester suites: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts for @implements format and mixed usage. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts for @implements deep validation, multi-story behavior, path validation, and error messages. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts for @implements being accepted as satisfying story/requirement presence. - Running `npm test -- --verbose` executes the Jest-based test suite (`jest --ci --bail --verbose` as configured in package.json) without any reported failures, indicating all these tests pass on this branch.
Traceability: - Implementation files add @story and @req annotations referencing docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md and the concrete REQ IDs from the story, e.g. src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts and src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts, providing clear bidirectional traceability.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT are implemented and verified. The plugin supports the `@implements ` format with detailed format validation, integrates @implements into both shallow format checks and deep requirement existence checks, and updates require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation so that @implements alone can satisfy their respective requirements. Mixed usage of @story, @req, and @implements is supported within the same code and comment blocks. Requirement IDs are scoped per story file, as demonstrated by multi-story tests that reuse the same ID across different story fixtures. Error messages for missing requirements and invalid paths include the story path being checked, matching the story’s error-context requirements. Extensive RuleTester coverage and rule documentation (valid-annotation-format.md and valid-req-reference.md) explicitly tie back to this story and its REQ IDs. Therefore, based on concrete implementation and passing tests, this story is assessed as fully PASSED.
